title: Fast Feathers, Slow Seeds
markdown:
Zuri loved finding out why things worked. Her best friend was Bloop, a round, shiny robot who was amazing at counting. *Beep boop! Whirr!* Bloop could count puffy clouds or even Zuri’s happy giggles!

One bright, sunny day in the park, Zuri and Bloop saw Coach Ellis. *TOOT TOOT!* went his whistle! As they walked, Zuri stopped. "Look!" she pointed.

There were two bird feeders hanging from a big, strong oak tree. One feeder was stuffed full of yummy seeds! It looked like a party for birds. But the other feeder? Oh no! It had just a tiny sprinkle of seeds way down at the bottom.

"Coach Ellis," Zuri asked, "why does one feeder have lots of seeds, and the other has only a few?"

Coach Ellis smiled a big smile. "What do you think?"

Zuri thought and thought. Bloop whirred, *Whirr?*

Suddenly, *WHOOSH!* Mr. Nutty the squirrel zoomed by! He was the park's super-speedy feeder-filler! He used two noisy, spinning machines. *Flick! Flick!* went the machine for the full feeder. It was so fast! Seeds flew out like confetti, filling that feeder in a flash! It was a seed-blitz!

But the other machine? It went *tick… tock… tick… tock.* It was so slow. *Tick… one seed! Toooock… another seed!* It was like a sleepy snail. It took a very, very long time to get just one little seed to pop out.

Zuri watched, her eyes wide like saucers. Bloop’s little light blinked faster and faster. *Boop! Boop! Boop!* He was counting!

Zuri pointed. "The fast machine went *Flick! Flick!* and lots of seeds came out super fast! It filled up all the way!" She then looked at the other feeder. "But the slow one went *tick… tock…* and only a little bit came out. It didn't fill up much at all."

Coach Ellis nodded kindly. "And what does that tell you about how fast the machines were going and how many seeds ended up in the feeders?"

Zuri’s brain did a happy little flip. "Oh! Fast machines put lots in! Slow machines put only a little!"

"That's right!" said Coach Ellis. "Fast means more seeds, and slow means less seeds! It’s like a science secret!"

Bloop beeped happily. *Boop! More seeds!* He pointed to the full feeder. *Beep! Less seeds!* He pointed to the nearly empty one.

Coach Ellis chuckled. "Exactly! When something happens quickly, you can get more of something. That’s why there are more seeds. When something happens slowly, you get less."

Zuri giggled again. "So, fast makes more, and slow makes less! It's like magic, but it's science!"

Bloop did a happy robot wiggle. *Boop! Faster means more! Beep! Slower means less!*

"Right!" said Coach Ellis. "It’s like running super-fast to the toy box – you can grab more toys than if you walk really slowly!"

Zuri imagined running like a zooming rocket, grabbing armfuls and armfuls of toys. She beamed. "I get it!"

"I wonder," Zuri said, her smart coder brain buzzing, "what else gets more when it goes fast, and less when it goes slow? Maybe how many bubbles I blow?"

Bloop beeped excitedly. *Boop! What else? Let’s count!*

As the sun painted the sky with pretty pink and orange colors, Zuri, Bloop, and Coach Ellis knew that watching birds eat was a big adventure. They had discovered the secret of more and less, all thanks to a speedy squirrel and a slow machine! What other secrets were hiding in plain sight?
characters: Zuri the little coder, Bloop the robot, Coach Ellis
